mula_devanagari: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः | मद्-भक्त एतद् विज्ञाय मद्-भावायोपपद्यते
mula_iast: iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ | mad-bhakta etad vijñāya mad-bhāvāyopapadyate
jayatirtha_prameyadipika: ।।13.19।।ननु ब्रह्मणि प्रतिपादिते केन साधनेनेदं बुद्ध्यारूढं भवेत् इत्याकाङ्क्षायां साधनं पश्चाद्वक्तव्यं तत्कुतः प्रथमत उक्तं इत्यत आह -- विकारे ति। विकारेष्वन्तर्भावं ज्ञापयितुं तदनन्तरमुपोद्धातप्रक्रिययोक्तमिति भावः। उद्देशक्रमानुसारेणयतश्च यत् [13।4] इति प्रथममनुक्त्वास च यो यत्प्रभावश्च [13।4] इत्येतत्कुत उक्तमित्यत आह -- बहुत्वादि ति। सूचीकटाहनिर्माणादौ बहुत्वस्य प्राथम्यव्यभिचाराद्धेत्वन्तरोक्तिः। अलौकिकस्य प्रभावस्य बुद्धयारोहे हि साधनानामत्युपयोगः? न तु तावान् लौकिकस्य प्रेरकत्वस्यानुभवारोह इति ज्ञापयितुं ज्ञानसाधनानन्तरमेव प्रभाव उक्तः। तत्प्रसङ्गेन चेति भावः।

current_dvaita_rendering.english: [Very thin bhāṣya.] The means of knowledge were stated first, because they are included among the modifications; their prominence comes from their number and their great usefulness as means.
current_dvaita_rendering.divergence_note: THIN: Madhva's supplied comment is two short, elliptical sentences about the ORDER of topics (why the means of knowledge were placed where they were, and why they are prominent). Rendering is tentative; 'vikārāntarbhāvāt' read as 'included among the modifications [of the field]'. He says nothing on mad-bhakta or mad-bhāva, so no Dvaita reading of the verse's soteriology is offered.

current_dvaita_everyday: Madhva's note only explains why the methods were listed where they were: there are many of them and they are very useful. In practice, a team lead should get the working habits written down before arguing about the mission statement. The note says nothing about devotion or the end goal, so neither should this application.

other_schools_english.advaita: Thus the field, from the great elements to dhṛti (fortitude), knowledge, from humility to the vision of the goal of true knowledge, and the knowable, ending with 'beyond tamas', have been told in brief; this much is the whole meaning of the Veda and of the Gītā, gathered up and told. Who is qualified for this samyag-darśana (right vision)? My bhakta (devotee), who has offered his whole being to Me, Vāsudeva, the omniscient Īśvara, the supreme Guru, his mind seized by the conviction 'whatever I see, hear or touch, all is Bhagavān Vāsudeva'. Knowing this right vision as taught, he becomes fit for mad-bhāva, My state, the state of paramātman (supreme Self), and goes to mokṣa (liberation).
other_schools_english.viśiṣṭādvaita: Thus the truth of the field has been told in brief, from 'the great elements, ahaṃkāra (ego-principle)' to 'aggregate, consciousness, fortitude'; the means of knowing the self that is to be known, from 'humility' to 'vision of the goal of true knowledge'; and the true nature of the knowable kṣetrajña (knower of the field), from 'beginningless, supreme' to 'set in the heart of all'. My devotee, knowing the true nature of the field, of the means to attain the self as distinct from the field, and of the knower of the field, becomes fit for mad-bhāva. My bhāva is My own nature, asaṃsāritva (freedom from transmigration); he becomes fit to attain that.
other_schools_english.śuddhādvaita: Opening with the verse 'Prakṛti and puruṣa both, the paramātman became of old; the form He took as His seat is called akṣara (the imperishable)', He sums up: from 'the great elements' to 'aggregate, consciousness, fortitude' the field has been told in brief; from 'humility' to 'vision of the goal of true knowledge', knowledge, which is also the means to knowing the self; and from 'beginningless, supreme' to 'set in the heart of all', the knowable, namely that Brahman is akṣara in nature. Only one who has bhakti (devotion) to Me, knowing all this, becomes fit for mad-bhāva, which means mad-guṇavattva (possessing My qualities).
other_schools_english.bhakti: He concludes the field and the rest, together with the qualified one and the fruit: thus the field, from the great elements to fortitude, knowledge, from humility to the vision of the goal of true knowledge, and the knowable, from 'beginningless supreme Brahman' to 'set in the heart'; what Vasiṣṭha and others taught at length, all of it I have told in brief. My bhakta (devotee), marked by the traits given in the previous chapter, knowing this, becomes fit for mad-bhāva, which is brahmatva (being Brahman).
other_schools_english.advaita-bhakti: Stating the qualified one and the fruit, He concludes: thus field, knowledge and knowable, drawn from Śruti and Smṛti, I have told in brief out of kindness to the slow of understanding, and this much is the whole meaning of the Veda and the Gītā; only My bhakta, marked as in the previous chapter, who has offered his whole being to Me, Bhagavān Vāsudeva, the supreme Guru, with Me as his sole refuge, is qualified. Knowing field, knowledge and knowable by discernment, he becomes fit for mad-bhāva, the state of supreme bliss empty of all harm, mokṣa (liberation), as the Śruti says 'to the great soul who has highest bhakti for God, and for the guru as for God, these teachings shine'. Therefore, always taking refuge in Me alone and seeking the highest goal of human life, one should keep to the means of self-knowledge, giving up the craving for trivial pleasures.
